properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 8259976
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/23/2025
Comments: On 12/23/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 33 degrees, overcast and lightly snowing when I arrived on location. Snowfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours, depositing approximately 3 inches on the location. The original south pad for the Taft 851 1V well has been returned to original grade. The plugged well monument witnessed during previous inspections was not visible. Stormwater diversion berms have been installed north and west of the original pad. Due to snow cover, stabilization could not be assessed for the constructed areas. Patterson drilling rig #805 has been towered down and removed from the north pad, having drilled eight new gas wells to total depth. Most of the drilling equipment has been removed from the site. Crews were on site, cleaning up the surface of the drilling mats and pumping out the well cellars. 40 frac tanks, seven rolloff dumpsters, two vac boxes, and four cement silos remain on site. Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Sand separators and two frac tanks remain attached to these wells. I did witness a 4' x 16' x 2" deep puddle of liquid on the unprotected pad surface north of the five GPUs that field tested at 1953 uS conductance. I reported this to a maintenance worker who relayed it to the Seneca site manager, Cory Miller.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water/ice. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1600 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/06/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8266448
Permit API: 015-24012
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/06/2026
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Blackhill Energy's Lee North well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 3/6/2026 at 0900 hours. The weather was 41 degrees F with cloudy skies and fog. A new Act 9 sign has been installed at the site entrance (photo #1). Site plans and an inspection log are held in the mailbox by the gate.New Spud dates for 3/3/2026 were recored for the Lee North 2H, 4H, 6H and 8H wells. A top-hole rig was observed drilling for the new wells' conductor casings. Topsoil has been piled on top of the pad's fill and cut slopes. The construction contractor plans to come back to rework the topsoil onto the slopes and construct the perimeter channels. Additional work is also necessary for the sediment basin. Recent thawing, snow melt and heavy rainfall has caused erosion and slumping on the pad's cut and fill slopes, stormwater channels and piled topsoils. Evidence of erosion can be seen in photos #5-7. Sediment laden fluids were observed flowing through the temporarily constructed stormwater channels and entering the sediment basin. The fluids in the basin then flowed into the skimmer and out of basin's outflow pipe. Sediment laden fluids were observed escaping the site's limit-of-disturbance (LOD) and into Wetland 4J (PEM) (photos #8 and 12). Photo #12 shows the observed sedimentation present in Wetland 4J. The planned rip rap apron below the sediment basin outflow pipe has not yet been constructed.The sediment laden fluids eventually flow downslope into Mill Creek. The DEP observed Mill Creek upstream and downstream of the sedimentation and Mill Creek appeared more turbid downstream of the sedimentation. Samples for Standard Analysis Code (SAC) 046 were collected from Mill Creek both upstream and downstream of the observed sedimentation. Photos #13 and 14 show samples #0983-523 and 524 next to the sample locations. The samples were collected to determine if Mill Creek was also impacted by the sedimentation.Based on the observed sediment laden fluids escaping the site's LOD and entering Wetland 4J, the following violations are cited against API #015-24012 at this time:25 Pa. Code 102.4(b)135 P.S. 691.401A representative with Blackhill Energy met onsite during this inspection. I explained my findings and the Blackhill Energy representative contacted the construction contractor to address the issues noted. The contractor planned to install some rock below the basin's outflow pipe to slow down some of the fluids and add silt sock to contain the sedimentation. I departed the site at 1150 hours.

Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was from the secondary containment of a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed through a culvert under the access road and continued to spread out and flow through vegetation approximately 400 feet. Moody & Associates has been employed to coordinate the clean-up of this crude oil release. Jordan Sipos, P.G. completed the testing to establish the extent of the release and contaminated soil. Clean-up of the contaminated soil has been ongoing and is nearly completed. Several piles of contaminated soil have been secured adjacent to the clean-up area until testing has been completed for disposal. Due to recent precipitation events removal of the remaining contaminated soil has been delayed. Work crew on site at the time of this inspection. The removal of the contaminated soil was completed with the least disturbance possible to the surrounding vegetation and without creating a muddy unstable area. Replacement of topsoil and vegetation of this area needs to be coordinated with landowner and State Forest representatives. Manifest for the removal and disposal of the contaminated soil need to be submitted to the Department to lift the violations associated with this release. 15 Day initial Response Letter received July 1, 2019 for Alternate Remediation provision found in the PA DEP Oil and Gas Spill Policy.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559). The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, corrosion, and possible failures. As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. The well is currently equipped for production. The well was currently producing off of the 6-5/8"x2" annulus and the 2" tubing was shut in. 2 check valves were in place on the production lines and were oriented correctly. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation. NO methane was detected in the slam bar holes utilizing a MSA ALTAIR 5X meter which was calibrated on 07/17/2023. No casing string pressures were observed at the time of inspection due to no pressure gauges in place and no operator provided well tender available. This well was labeled with an incorrect well API#, this issue was brought to the attention of the operator and promptly fixed. Further inspections of this well may be warranted to determine the root cause of the complaint.

Permit API: 083-50409
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Wetmore Twp

Inspection Date: 3/26/2021
Comments: This spill occurred sometime in the previous few months but was not reported to DEP. It was noted on a routine inspection by WQSS Rob Bechtel and myself en route to check another site. It appears as though a line leaked and allowed an unknown quantity of crude oil to be released to the site. Some volume flowed off the site and entered a spring run/UNT of Twomile Run. Crude oil was apparent in pools in several areas and fresher product was caught in moss lining the channel of the spring. It then appears to have flowed some 300 feet and entered another UNT of Twomile Run. The operator placed a boom in this stream at some point prior to the discovery of this spill by myself. Some sheen was apparent in leaf piles at this point, but no fresh product was noted. The operator was contacted and they were on the lease at the time. Immediate cleanup options were discussed, including installation of two siphon dams in the initial spring run and use of absorbent pads to catch any oil seeping from the banks. Further inspection will be performed as necessary. Violations are noted.

Comments: On January 6, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an administrative inspection for a spill at the Inflection Energy Hensler Well Pad. On January 5, 2022, around 2140, Zac Subra reported a spill of approximately 30 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the well pad surface. At about 920 on January 6, 2022, DEP spoke with Zac Subra on the phone. Mr. Subra said a hydraulic fluid line on a water truck ruptured and caused the spill. Inflection contractors began removing the hydraulic fluid and excavating the impacted soil immediately. Inflection contractors excavated an area of about 20 ft. X 15 ft. of the pad surface. Due to the ground being frozen, Inflection contractors only had to scrape the top of the pad surface to remove the impacted soil in the previously noted area. The impacted soil was added to a rolloff dumpster and hauled to a landfill. Inflection then went back to the pad during the day to verify that the impacted soil had been completely removed. Zac said a small amount of remaining soil had to be removed at this time since it was not observed earlier in the morning. The small amount of soil was added to barrels and is awaiting approval to be disposed of. Inflection then backfilled the excavated area with clean fill. Photos of the area excavated and clean up were provided by Inflection Energy. The spill of hydraulic fluid outside of containment is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.54. The violations have been immediately corrected.

Comments: Arrived onsite at 10:43 in response to a spill notification received on 12/3/18 at 15:45. Peg Farrell reported a release of about 25 gallons of brine water off of containment at the northeast corner of the pad near the produced water tanks and sand vac. The impacted area included a portion of the a collection ditch at the edge of the pad. Chief was in the process of stimulating the 4H well. Met with Colter, Company Man onsite and Kellon, Environmental Field Coordinator. They believed the cause of the spill to be from an overflowed blender. The overflow then leaked through containment and onto the pad surface. There are two layers of containment under the equipment (plastic, felt, plastic, felt). Chief will continue to inspect the containment during operations and repair any punctures or tears found. The vac truck onsite removed pooled water from the containment as soon as the spill was noticed. At the time of inspection an excavator was removing the impacted area of the pad. The area being excavated was approximately 8 ft. wide, 15 ft. long, and 2 in. deep (Photo #1). At the time of inspection about 10 to 15 cubic feet of soil had been removed. It was expected that 20 to 25 cubic feet would be removed in total. A Hanna Instruments Soil Conductivity Tester (S/N: L02110754) was used to screen the nearby area and it appeared that contamination was limited to the area immediately around the excavation (Photos #2, 3). The 5H well is scheduled to be stimulated following the 4H. Operations are expected to be completed Sunday afternoon (12/9/18). Chief is planning to pull additional containment under the blender and around the contaminated area the following Monday or Tuesday (12/10 or 12/11) to conduct additional screening of the pad surface. Violations noted and immediately corrected.

Barium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential Medium Specific Concentration (MSC) for groundwater of 2,000 micrograms per liter (µg/l) with a concentration of 33,570 µg/l detected in the Department’s sample and 34,500 µg/l detected in SWNPC's sample. Aluminum was detected above the Act 2 Secondary Maximum Contaminant Level (SMCL) of 200 µg/l with a concentration of 9,581 µg/l detected in the Department’s sample and 12,500 µg/l detected in SWNPC's sample. Chloride was detected above the Act 2 SMCL of 250,000 µg/l with a concentration of 1,511,000 µg/l detected in the Department’s sample and 1,470,000 µg/l detected in SWNPC's sample. Iron was detected above the Act 2 SMCL of 300 µg/l with a concentration of 23,970 µg/l detected in the Department’s sample and 22,600 µg/l detected in SWNPC's sample. Manganese was detected above the Act 2 SMCL of 50 µg/l with a concentration of 1,657 µg/l detected in the Department’s sample and 1,560 µg/l detected in SWNPC's sample. Bromide was detected at a concentration of 13,343 µg/l in the Department’s sample and 7,910 µg/l detected in SWNPC's sample. Calcium was detected at a concentration of 293,000 µg/l in the Department’s sample and 280,000 µg/l detected in SWNPC's sample. SWNPC's background soil sample collected at the Moore Pad exhibited a concentration of Arsenic of 7.48 mg/kg. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow-up after the Department discovered fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC) in the northwest stormwater channel. Two workover rigs are in operation on the well pad. I met with company man Marc McCartor upon arriving on location. He informed me that no excavation had taken place yet in the northwest stormwater channel. He said a sump was installed at the west corner at the end of the stormwater channel. He said that a vacuum truck is on site sucking up the fluid from the channel and the sump. The EC of the fluid in the sump near the halfway point of the northwest pad edge was 333 uS/cm. Farther west, the EC of the fluid in the channel near the location of the sample taken in the previous inspection on 5/8/24 was 798 uS/cm. Farther west within the channel, the EC was 2.34 mS/cm. In the sump at the west corner of the pad within the liner, the EC of the fluid was 2.01 mS/cm. Under the liner, the EC of the fluid was 1600 uS/cm.The Department recommends continuing to collect and dispose of the fluid in the northwest stormwater channel and in the sump. I made this recommendation to the company man before leaving the location. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21946 for the elevated electrical conductivity fluid discovered by the Department in the northwest stormwater channel on 5/8/24.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21938 for the reported release of produced fluid to the pad surface on 3/1/24.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-05-01 to Msl Oil & Gas Corp in Hamilton Twp, McKean county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Msl Oil & Gas Corp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-05-01
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 883844
Permit API: 083-47035
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-05-01
Comments: Brian Ayers of DEP was contacted by MSL's Dick Pascarella on 4/23/2020 regarding a condensate leak from a tank that was found that day. PA Fish and Boat Commission officer Tom Mcmann was on site 4/24/2020 to follow up and took some photos that are included in this report. It appears as though a small, uncontained drip gas tank had a failure at a fitting at some point prior to the spill being found. This tank holds mostly water that condenses from the gas coming from the compressor station nearby, but also contains some condensed petroleum liquids. An estimated 5-10 gallons of this fluid escaped from the broken fitting and was spilled to the ground. Some of this ran down slope toward an UNT of Chappel Fork, with some collecting in a low, wet area and a small amount eventually entering the water. Tom Mcmann documented photos of the condensate in the vernal pool area, which is included in the attached photos. A Department site visit was performed 5/1/2020. The operator has scraped up the surface of the contaminated site, and placed down straw mulch and seed. They also put down gravel around equipment close to the stream and have built containment around the drip gas tank. The area close to the stream was observed to have a strong condensate odor and some sheen could be spotted entering the stream when this area was agitated on the stream banks. Some product was noted, mostly in the form of sheen, in the UNT Chappel Fork. The stream crosses Chappel Fork Rd a few feet from where the product entered, and sheen was visible upon agitation approximately 150-200 feet downstream. No free product was apparent and no other waters were impacted. The operator was contacted and instructed to place booms for containment and monitor through the weekend, followed by a run of agitating the stream bottom to push any product caught in the substrate to collect it in the next week. They also dug up the impacted soil next to the stream with shovels and removed it. Bill Otto of MSL sent photos to show that booms were placed and digging done as of late Friday, May 1. Further followup will be done as possible.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RICE DRILLING B LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/18/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8153115
Permit API: 125-27720
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: North Bethlehem Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/18/2023
Comments: On 07/18/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the Ironman Well Site in response to an incident report received by the Department and submitted by EQT on 07/17/2023 (CTS: 373620). I was accompanied by Matt Dracup, PGM (PADEP), Doug Oberdorf, and Jason Nicholson (EQT). Additional EQT and SPSI representatives on site. Stressed vegetation observed on north-northwest facing slope (fill side) of the Ironman pad on 07/14/2023 by an EQT contractor doing a routine site inspection. EQT representative investigated stressed vegetation on 07/17/2023 and identified it as a brine release and notified the Department. It was further investigated by EQT on 07/17/2023 w/ interim remediation activities starting on 07/18/2023. According to EQT, an approx. 5 ft x 2 ft pool of fluid was observed within area of stressed vegetation and fluid was observed sprinkling out. The overall area of stressed vegetation was approximately 25 ft x 25 ft. The release was estimated over a barrel and Act 2 remediation is anticipated. The source of the leak was identified as a small pinhole in cushion elbow at the northern most corner of the pad from the buried common dump line transferring brine flowback from the GPUs to the ASTs; approx. 70 ft northeast, away from the stressed vegetation area. Operator discovery and pre-remediation conductivity levels and incident writeup requested.Inspection observations: Area of stressed vegetation and pooled production fluid observed on fill slope below northwestern edge of pad and below compressor building on the pad. Among pooled fluid, an oily sheen was also observed. The impacted area appeared to be approx. 25 ft. x 25 ft. The area was covered with a plastic tarp upon arriving on site (Photos 1-7). SPSI crew preparing and beginning excavation to locate source of leak and begin remediation measures. Potholes to be dug on pad around approximate area of leak source to gain extent of fluid. Elevated conductivity observed within impacted area yielded readings of 14.62 mS, 9.96 mS. Readings beyond edge of impacted area, on the more northern edge of the area, displayed a reading of 1.87 mS. Additional readings within vegetation beyond edge of affected area were taken and yielded levels of 1.03 and within the area beyond the fence approximately 5 ft. at the bottom of the slope, 1.98 mS was observed within vegetation. Readings taken within the Unnamed Tributary to Daniels Run, below impacted area approximately 125 ft. north of the impacted area. Readings obtained within water and sediment of the stream w/ levels at 0.43-0.86 mS. Readings obtained within retentive berm along southeastern edge of site below pad; readings taken in water and within sediment yielded 0.33 mS and 0.60 mS (8-16). Readings taken at southern corner of the vegetated swales outlet structure, both in and around; readings of 0.46 mS within water and 0.59 mS within mud around the structure observed (17). SPSI began excavating a pothole, approx. 3 ft in depth; pooled fluid observed within. Conductivity reading within excavated hole was 6.30 mS. Vegetated berm adjacent to hole, above impacted area, displayed a reading of 0.34 mS (18-20). Additional readings within vegetation beyond western edge of impacted area displayed 2.21-6.44 mS (21-23). Reading in fluid contained within secondary containment around ASTs w/ level of 7.20 mS. Due to observed release of production fluid within vegetation on site and potential for fluid to impact WOC downslope of impacted area, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued. Additional violations of 78a.66(b)(2) for failure to report within 2 hours, 78a.66(b)1(i), 78a.66(b)1(ii), and 91.33(a) for threatening WOC pollution, 5 gallons not completely contained and failure to report to DEP and downstream users are being issued. Additional follow up inspections to be conducted to monitor WOC downslope of impacted area.

No fluid or gas leaks detected on site at the time of inspection. Request operator verify open or closed status of surface casing. Operator in violation of : OGA3220(A)-Plugging Requirements.
